extracted_information: The Microsoft Learn article "Working with WMI - PowerShell" provides a comprehensive guide on leveraging Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) within PowerShell. It details the use of both older, deprecated WMI cmdlets (found in Windows PowerShell 5.1) and the recommended Common Information Model (CIM) cmdlets (introduced in PowerShell 3.0 and prevalent in PowerShell 6+). The guide covers local WMI queries, performance optimization, and advanced techniques for querying remote computers, including handling access permissions using CIM sessions and choosing between WSMan (default) and DCOM protocols.

powershell_versions_supported.powershell_3_0_and_newer: Introduced CIM cmdlets, recommended for new development.
powershell_versions_supported.powershell_6_and_newer: WMI cmdlets are deprecated, CIM cmdlets are the standard.

wsman.requirements: Remote computer needs PowerShell version 3.0 or higher with WSMan stack version 3.0.

dcom.description: Alternative protocol for older Windows versions (e.g., Windows Server 2000) where PowerShell might not be installed. Requires New-CimSessionOption -Protocol Dcom. Often blocked by firewalls on newer Windows.
dcom.compatibility: Allows Get-CimInstance to communicate with Windows versions as old as Windows Server 2000.

features.name: WMI Cmdlets (Deprecated in PowerShell 6+)
features.description: Native cmdlets available in Windows PowerShell. For new development, CIM cmdlets are recommended.

features.name: CIM Cmdlets (Recommended)
features.description: Introduced in PowerShell 3.0, grouped in the CimCmdlets module. Still allow interaction with WMI.

optimization.property_selection: Use -Property parameter with Get-CimInstance to limit retrieved data, improving efficiency for remote queries. Example: Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_BIOS -Property SerialNumber
optimization.output_formatting: Pipe to Select-Object -Property to get specific properties, or Select-Object -ExpandProperty to return property as a string. Dotted syntax also returns a string (e.g., (Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_BIOS -Property SerialNumber).SerialNumber).

methods.note: Can result in 'Access is denied' if current user lacks rights. Relaunching PowerShell as domain admin is not recommended due to security implications.

methods.method: Using CIM Sessions (Recommended for efficiency and credential management)
steps: Create a CIM session with New-CimSession, specifying -ComputerName and -Credential (e.g., using Get-Credential). Example: $CimSession = New-CimSession -ComputerName dc01 -Credential (Get-Credential)
Use the created CIM session with Get-CimInstance via the -CimSession parameter. Example: Get-CimInstance -CimSession $CimSession -ClassName Win32_BIOS
methods.benefits: More efficient for multiple queries to the same machine as connection is set up once. Allows specifying alternate credentials per command using principle of least privilege.

methods.method: Using DCOM Protocol for Older Systems
steps: Create a DCOM session option: $DCOM = New-CimSessionOption -Protocol Dcom
Create a CIM session using the DCOM option and credentials: $CimSession = New-CimSession -ComputerName sql03 -SessionOption $DCOM -Credential $Cred
methods.use_case: For connecting to remote computers running older Windows versions (e.g., Windows Server 2008 non-R2) without PowerShell installed, or when WSMan is not available/configured.

actions.output_details: Shows Id, Name, InstanceId, ComputerName, and Protocol (WSMAN or DCOM).
